correctness.rationale: A witness assigns opposing colors to each letter occurrences. Nested intervals obstruct equality; for FIFO first/second occurrence orders, crossings force same first-color assignments, so a crossing graph has exactly 2^(components-1) unordered witnesses. In a primitive Dyck excursion, each interval after the first begins before an earlier interval closes and hence crosses one, giving connected components equal to excursions. Primitive Catalan generating function P=zC gives [z^q]P^r via Lagrange inversion, all moments via 1/(1-2^s P), and simple pole rho=3/16 yields the stated q^(3/2)(4/3)^q second moment. Independently enumerated every double-occurrence word for q<=4 and directly counted unordered position bipartitions: complete histograms agreed.

final_claim: For words with exactly two copies of each of q distinct letters, all shuffle-square witnesses (unordered position bipartitions) number 2^(r-1), where r counts primitive Dyck excursions in the matching first/second-order word. The full labeled multiplicity histogram is q! * r/(2q-r) * binom(2q-r,q), with mean (q+1)/2, exponentially growing second moment, and tight fixed-excursion limiting law.
limitations: Exactly two occurrences per symbol, q>=1, linear labeled words and unordered position partitions.
